<div align=center>

# Agentforce Vibes Extension

</div>

Agentforce Vibes extension is an AI-powered developer tool that's enhanced with premium third-party models. The extension provides intelligent coding support while ensuring that customer data is never used for training. 

Head over to the [Agentforce Vibes Extension Documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/tools/vscode/en/einstein/einstein-overview) to learn more.

**Note**: Agentforce Vibes extension uses generative AI, which can produce inaccurate or harmful responses. The output generated by AI is often nondeterministic. Before using the generated output, review it for accuracy and safety. You assume responsibility for how the outcomes of Agentforce are applied to your organization.

## Get Started

Agentforce Vibes extension is available in the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=salesforce.salesforcedx-einstein-gpt) and the [Open VSX Registry](https://open-vsx.org/extension/salesforce/salesforcedx-einstein-gpt) and as a part of the [Salesforce Extension Pack](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=salesforce.salesforcedx-vscode).

Go to [Agentforce Vibes Extension Set Up Documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/tools/vscode/en/einstein/einstein-setup) for setup instructions.

Agentforce Vibes extension is enabled by default. You can easily disable or uninstall the Agentforce Vibes extension at any time. Bring up the Extensions view by clicking on the Extensions icon in the Activity Bar on the side of VS Code or the **View: Show Extensions** command (⇧⌘X). Search for "Agentforce Vibes" in installed extensions list, and then select **Disable** or **Uninstall**.

## What can Agentforce Vibes Do?

With Agentforce Vibes, you can build and deploy UIs with a prompt. Check out these sample prompts.

- Build a todo app with an Apex controller and LWC component. Use the Todo__c object.
- Create an LWC component that displays account names, revenue, and associated contact names.
- Add a property assistant agent to the dashboard to track applications and maintenance requests.

Use Agentforce Vibes extension to enhance developer productivity.

## Neovim plugin (this fork)

This fork adds **einstein.nvim**, a dependency-free Neovim (>= 0.10) port of the
portable core of the extension. It is one codebase in a standard plugin layout
(`plugin/` + `lua/einstein/`), consumable by vim.pack, lazy.nvim, and LuaRocks.
The VS Code extension above remains the full product; this plugin covers only
the flows that ride the Einstein GPT gateway directly.

### What it does

The plugin talks to the same gateway the extension uses:

- `POST {base}/chat/generations` where `{base}` defaults to
  `https://api.salesforce.com/ai/gpt/v1` (test/stage/perf/dev hosts are
  selectable via the `environment` option).
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <org access token>`,
  `x-sfdc-app-context: EinsteinGPT`, `x-sfdc-core-tenant-id: <org id>`, and
  `x-client-feature-id` when configured.
- The bearer token is resolved at runtime from your Salesforce CLI session
  (`sf org display --json`) or from `EINSTEIN_SF_ACCESS_TOKEN` (with optional
  `EINSTEIN_SF_TENANT_ID`). It is never stored, logged, or shown; when no
  session exists, every command fails closed with a structured
  `not_authenticated` error.

Commands: `:EinsteinChat`, `:EinsteinGenerate`, `:EinsteinExplain`,
`:EinsteinGenerateTests` (Apex test classes and LWC Jest tests, mirroring this
repo's test case generation docs), `:EinsteinAuth`, `:EinsteinModels`.

Out of scope, because they are VS Code-host surfaces with no gateway
equivalent: the chat sidebar webview, the orchestration/task board, inline
autocomplete (editor completion provider), Dev Agent conversations, and the
MCP/skills settings UIs.

### Install with vim.pack

```lua
vim.pack.add({ 'https://github.com/qompassai/Einstein-GPT-for-Developers' })
require('einstein').setup({})
```

### Install with lazy.nvim

```lua
{
  'qompassai/Einstein-GPT-for-Developers',
  config = function()
    require('einstein').setup({})
  end,
}
```

### Install with LuaRocks

```sh
luarocks make einstein-scm-1.rockspec
```

```lua
require('einstein').setup({
  -- model = 'sfdc_ai__DefaultBedrockAnthropicClaude46Sonnet', -- default
  -- environment = 'prod',        -- prod | test | stage | perf | dev
  -- sf_target_org = 'my-org',    -- optional sf --target-org
  -- feature_id = '...',          -- optional x-client-feature-id
})
```

Generated code comes from a nondeterministic model; review it before use,
exactly as with the VS Code extension.
